A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RE-VDM with matching authors, method and principal experiments. All supplied pages, including v2's supplementary Sections 8–14, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative interpolation results on BS-ERGB, HQF and Clear-Motion in Table 2, alongside qualitative results and a VAE reconstruction experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline results, component ablations, generation results and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the frozen video diffusion model, trainable event-conditioning components, multi-stack event representation, tiled denoising and Two-side Fusion. The supplementary implementation disclosures do not establish a changed algorithm or training objective.

E1.justification: v2 newly evaluates single-frame, event-guided video generation/extrapolation in Section 9; v1 described this capability but reported interpolation evaluations. BS-ERGB, HQF and Clear-Motion remain the datasets used.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds DynamiCrafter, PerVFI, InterpAny-Clearer, EMA-VFI and GIMM-VFI-R-P while retaining Time Reversal, RIFE and CBMNet-Large. This substantially broadens the evaluated frame-only and video-diffusion comparisons. Several qualitative comparisons also replace or supplement RIFE with these methods.

E3.justification: The main benchmark metrics, skip counts, VAE processing and dataset-specific upsampling factors remain unchanged. New experiments compare endpoint availability and upsampling factors of 1, 1.5 and 2. Section 14 introduces efficiency measurements on one RTX 4090, using 1024 × 576 outputs and runtime averaged over 16 frames.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained VAE illustration in Figure 5, v2 adds quantitative and qualitative tests of Two-side Fusion and input upsampling (Tables 3 and 5; Figures 9, 10 and 13). It also adds hallucination/error-accumulation case studies and computational analysis in Table 6, substantially strengthening component validation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new runtime averaging over 16 frames describes the evaluation procedure, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All existing Table 2 scores are unchanged, but v2 adds five baselines' scores, ablation results, efficiency measurements and revised qualitative comparisons. New BS-ERGB results include generation/interpolation PSNR of 25.79/27.74 in Table 3 and 1×/2× upsampling PSNR of 24.82/27.74 in Table 5; these compare experimental conditions rather than version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 retain the same diffusion formulation, tile accumulation and temporal fusion mathematics. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations appear in the supplement.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the claims of first adapting pretrained video diffusion models to EVFI and achieving strong generalization and frame consistency. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of hallucination and accumulated errors in one-sided generation, acknowledges frame-only methods' better LPIPS despite reconstruction problems, and explicitly discusses computational cost. The existing explanations based on pretrained priors and limitations involving VAE detail loss and smoothing remain.

D1.justification: Sections 10 and 13 newly document Clear-Motion capture hardware, alignment and sequence inventory, AdamW settings, 72-hour training, 512 × 320 tiles, 0.1 overlap and 25 denoising steps. Existing batch-size and training-GPU information is relocated. Although the explicit VAE downsampling/channel-count sentence is removed from Section 3.4, reproducibility documentation expands substantially.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the new baselines, TimeRewind, HR-INR, AdamW and additional event-camera research, while removing the EV-IMO and 0-MMS references. These broaden supporting literature without substantially changing the related-work narrative or central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 revises the evaluation discussion, adds an ablation subsection and a structured supplement, and moves training details into that supplement. The main section order and most abstract, introduction, method and conclusion wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains substantial comparator rows and ranking colors, and Tables 3–6 add ablation, dataset and efficiency displays. New figures illustrate generation failures, capture hardware and upsampling. The teaser and several comparison panels change, while matched qualitative examples are reorganized between the main paper and supplement.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation and reporting gaps: broader baseline comparisons test competitiveness, Tables 3 and 5 directly evaluate key design choices, and Sections 10 and 13 substantially improve reproducibility information. Table 6 and the expanded limitations also expose the considerable runtime cost. Together these substantially strengthen the evidence and transparency of the unchanged method; original benchmark scores remain unchanged and uncertainty estimates remain absent.
